arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Clement argued that taxpayer standing is narrow. He cited Flast v. Cohen. He stated that standing applies to congressional spending.
Justice Scalia questioned the consistency of the position. He noted the establishment clause concern in both cases.
Justice Ginsburg asked if standing exists for congressional legislation. She compared it to the executive order in question.
General Clement argued that denying standing does not stop lawsuits. He noted that directly injured plaintiffs can still sue.
